links.outcome: Patient perceptions and appointment intention by AI disclosure type (administrative, diagnostic, therapeutic, non-AI) and condition severity
links.effect: Administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI. High severity amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, and explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity.
links.quote: These findings suggest that AI disclosure in digital medicine should distinguish administrative from clinical uses and be calibrated to clinical severity, while highlighting the need for preregistered replication using behavioral outcomes.

links.effect: In 1574 adults, administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic/therapeutic AI; high severity amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI.
links.quote: High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity.

links.effect: High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI; explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity, mediated by competence, trust, and empathy.
